summary: Signing users in with LinkedIn and posting on a member's behalf are self-serve. Almost everything else, including advertising, community management, sales and talent features, requires LinkedIn to approve you, and the pages read publish no review time.

verdict.headline: Sign in and share are self-serve. Anything beyond them depends on LinkedIn approving you, with no published timeline and no guarantee even if you meet the requirements.

effort.label: A day for self-serve products. Approval programs add open-ended back and forth

prerequisites.detail: Products are added on the app's Products tab. The pages read do not describe how the app is created or what it must be linked to.

prerequisites.item: A clear answer on which product you need
prerequisites.detail: Self-serve permissions or an approval-only program. This decides everything about timing.

steps.title: Create a LinkedIn developer app
steps.detail: This is the starting point. The pages read do not cover app creation, so follow the Developer Portal prompts and see the uncertainties below.

steps.title: Add the self-serve products
steps.detail: profile and email (Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect) and w_member_social (Share on LinkedIn) are open to all developers.

steps.title: Decide whether you need an approval-only product
steps.detail: Advertising, Sales Navigator, Talent and Learning products need approval or a partner application. Compliance permissions are closed.

steps.title: Apply and plan around the tiers
steps.detail: Advertising and Community Management start at a Development tier. Move to Standard with a support ticket (advertising) or app review (community management).

steps.title: Register your redirect URL
steps.detail: It must be an absolute HTTPS URL registered on the app's Auth tab, without a fragment.

steps.title: Build the 3-legged OAuth flow
steps.detail: Send an unpredictable state, request the fewest scopes, and exchange the code within 30 minutes. Members consent to all scopes together.

steps.title: Plan for 60-day tokens
steps.detail: Access tokens last 60 days. Programmatic refresh is limited to certain partners, so most apps rerun the authorization redirect.

limits.title: Community Management development tier
limits.detail: 500 calls per app and 100 per member per 24 hours, and testing must be finished within 12 months of access.

limits.title: Changing scopes forces re-authentication
limits.detail: Members consent to all requested scopes together.

limits.title: Marketing API version sunset
limits.detail: Version 202511 is scheduled to sunset on 2026-11-16, so move to a current versioned API.

blockers.problem: LinkedIn does not approve your application
blockers.why: LinkedIn selects partners at its discretion and may decline even when you meet the minimum requirements.
blockers.nextMove: Build what the self-serve products allow first, and apply with a precise description of your use case.

blockers.problem: You cannot tell when approval will come
blockers.why: The pages read state no review timeline for the Standard tier, and restricted APIs have no fixed timeline.
blockers.nextMove: Keep a self-serve version shippable and ask Developer Support for status.

blockers.problem: Users have to sign in again every 60 days
blockers.why: Access tokens last 60 days and programmatic refresh is for a limited set of partners.
blockers.nextMove: Rerun the authorization redirect before expiry. It skips consent when the member is still logged in.

blockers.problem: Development tier limits stop your testing
blockers.why: Community Management development access is capped on calls and requires you to finish within 12 months.
blockers.nextMove: Apply for Standard early and design tests around the caps.

agentCanDo: Compare your feature list against the self-serve and approval-only products
Draft the use-case description for the approval application
Write the authorization redirect, state check, code exchange and 60-day re-auth flow
Create the Composio auth config once you have a client ID and secret
youMustDo: Create the developer app and add products while signed in to LinkedIn
Submit support tickets and partner applications and answer LinkedIn's questions
Provide any company information LinkedIn asks for

uncertainties: The pages read do not describe how to create a LinkedIn developer app, or whether it must be associated with a company page or verified by a page admin.
No review timeline is stated for the Standard tier or for most partner programs.
The authorization page's scope example uses older scope names. Confirm current names in the Developer Portal.
